All procuring entities are hereby advised to follow the below set of guidelines, and all ad ministrative departments are asked to circulate this advisory among their subordinate offices. General Guidelines: Minor (Non-Material) Deviation: Means any deviation that does not materially alter or depar t from the characteristics, terms, conditions, and other requirements set out in the bidding docu ment. A minor or nonmaterial error or omission constitutes an oversight in the bidding docume nt that can be corrected without any changes in the substance of the bid. Handling Minor Non-Conformities: In case of minor non-conformities, the Bid Evaluation Commit tee shall seek information and documents with respect to those non-conformities which are hist orical in nature. Example: Missing pages/attachments, illegibility in a submitted document, non -submission of the requisite number of copies, or missing documents issued by an authority. Substantive Changes Prohibited: No substantive changes to qualification information or to a submission— including changes aimed at making an unqualified bidder qualified or an unrespon sive submission responsive— shall be sought, offered, or permitted under any circumstances. E xample: If a bidder has not submitted the Manufacturer's Authorization Letter (which is an eligib ility criterion) along with the bid, the same should NOT be requested as a minor deficiency to q ualify the bidder. Historical Documents Only: Shortfall information or documents should be sought ONLY in th e case of historical documents that pre-existed at the time of the tender opening and have not u ndergone changes since then. These should be called only based on the recommendations of th e Tender Committee. Examples: Audited Statement of Accounts, PAN Card, GST Registration Ce rtificate, Incorporation/Registration Certificate, etc. Related Shortfall Documents: Regarding qualification criteria, after the submission of the ten der, only related shortfall documents may be asked for and considered. Example: If the bidder h as submitted a supply/service order without its completion/performance certificate, the certifica te can be requested and considered. However, no NEW supply/service order may be requested

to qualify the bidder. Deficiencies Apparent from Bid: The procuring entity can only seek documents and informat ion pertaining to a minor deficiency that is apparent from the bid already submitted. Example: If the bidder has not submitted the turnover certificate, it cannot be sought under Rule 23(15) of t he Assam Public Procurement Rules, 2020, as this cannot be interpreted as a minor deficiency. However, if the bidder submitted the turnover certificate but failed to submit the Audited State ment of Accounts, the statement can be sought.
